So, from the statements of those application it is clearly divulged that the petitioner suppressed the facts. Moreso, the notices (a) [Lists of] buildings the possession of which have been taken as abandoned property under the President's. Order: (b) [Lists of buildings in respect of which notices] for surrendering or taking possession as abandoned property under the said Order have been issued: Provided the no such list shall include any building in respect of which— (a) any decree or order has been passed, at any time before the publication of the list in the official Gazette, by any court declaring the building not to be an abandoned property or not to have [been] vested in the Government under the President's Order or declaring the possession by the Government of the building as an abandoned property under that Order to be illegal or invalid or directing the Government or any officer or authority subordinate to it to return, restore or transfer the building to any person, or (b) a suit, appeal, application or other legal proceeding is pending before any court, immediately before the date of publication of the list in the official Gazette, in which the vesting in, or possession of, the government of the building as abandoned property under the President's Order has been called in question in any manner whatsoever or any prayer has been made for return, restoration or transfer of the building by the Government or by any officer or authority subordinate to it to any person. (2) The list published under sub-section (1) shall be conclusive evidence of the fact that the buildings the buildings included therein are abandoned property and have [been] vested in the Government as such. 20. On perusal of the application under section 7 of the Ordinance filed by the respondent No. 2 in the Settlement's Court it appears that the petitioner did not mention in the application that earlier he had filed the suit before the Civil Court for the same purpose. It is also revealed from the judgment of the Settlement's Court that the respondent No. 2 as petitioner neither examined by the said Court on oath to satisfy the Court itself in accordance with law that he was in Bangladesh from 25th March, 1971 to 28-2-1972 and manage, control and supervise the properties in question nor he produced any documents exhibiting the same in Court in accordance with law, Even then, the Court of Settlement opined that since the properties in question were enlisted as abandoned properties in violation of the proviso (b) of the section 5(1) of the Ordinance, hence, properties must be released and excluded from the "Ka" list of the abandoned properties which is unfounded and superfluous as no evidences were lead to prove any such violation. The properties in question were listed as abandoned properties as per meaning of Article 2(1) of the President Order-16 of 1972 and same had listed as abandoned property in the year of 1972 and vested in the Government. Therefore, those were listed under section 5(1) (a) (b) of the Abandoned buildings (Supplementary provisions) Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 which does not come within the purview of proviso (b) of section 5(1) (a) of the Ordinance unless it is proved that the Government had the knowledge about the proceedings in any Court and the plea of the pending suit was not proved in accordance with law before the Court of Settlement. 21. Furthermore, it is clearly proved that the Court of Settlement without taking any evidence to that effect opined that the enlisting the properties in the "Ka" list has done in violation of the proviso (b) of the section 5(1) of the Ordinance. 22. We are of the view that since it is admitted facts that there is a suit before promulgating the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985, therefore it is crystal clear that the respondent No. 2 himself suppressed the events of filing of the suit. More-so, at the time of listing the properties in the year 1972 nor in the year 1984 raised any legal and lawful objection in accordance with law. Though notices were served in those addresses to reply. More-so, the point raised in the application under section 7 of the Ordinance also not proved before the Court of Settlement which calls for interference by this Court. On the other hand he filed the application in the Settlement Court which was not proved by giving evidence through competent witness and documents. 23. In that view of the matter we are of the considered view that the Court of Settlement passed the impugned judgment and order without its jurisdiction which cannot be sustained in law and, as such, the same is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 24. We find support of our view to the case Government of Bangladesh and another vs Mohiuddin reported in 15 BLC (AD) 179, to the case of Abu Taker vs Bangladesh reported in 14 BLC (AD) 19. 25. In such of view the matter and discussion all the Rule Nisi are made absolute. 26. The judgment and order passed by the First Court of Settlement dated 14-10-1992 in Settlement Case Nos. 48 of 1992, 49 of 1992, 50 of 1992 and 652 of 1988 are hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect, however, without any order as to cost. 27. The direction to exclude the properties from the "Ka" list is hereby recalled. Communicate this judgment at once. End.

caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 185 of 2025 with Civil Rule No. 735 (FM) of 2024)
lawyer:
Md. Sheikh Awsafur Rahman, Senior Advocate with AKM Ashiful Haque and Eeshith Monzul Shohiny, Advocates—For the Appellant. 
Monjur Elahi Porag, Advocate—For the Respondents.
parties:
Zarrin Suba ------ Applicant-Appellant Md. Bashir Ullah
VS
National Credit and Judgment Commerce Bank Limited 10th July, 2025 1 and others ------ Opposite Parties-Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Bashir Ullah, J: Since the point of law and facts so figured in the appeal and the Rule are intertwined, those have been heard together and are being disposed of by this common judgment. 

2. At the instance of the applicant in Miscellaneous Case No. 06 of 2024 preferred under section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, read with Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, this appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 28-10-2024, passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka disallowing the same on contest. 

3. The short facts leading to preferring this appeal are:—
The applicant purchased the suit Flat No. 2-B, measuring 2353.32 square feet from opposite party No. 3, (Amena Islam) by a Sale Deed No. 3852 dated 2-9-2020 and took possession of the property completing all legal requirements and formalities of Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (RAJUK) and other government authorities. While in possession of the disputed property, the applicant mutated her name with RAJUK and also with the office of the Assistant Commissioner (Land). The applicant has been paying land development tax for the disputed flat regularly. Prior to the sale of the disputed property to the applicant, her vendor, Amena Islam (Opposite Party No. 3), applied to RAJUK on 8-12-2019 seeking permission to sell the disputed flat to the applicant, whereupon, RAJUK duly granted permission to sell the disputed flat. While the applicant was enjoying peaceful possession in the disputed flat, all of a sudden, she received a Legal Notice dated 4-11-2020 issued by one, Mr. Nasir Uddin, Advocate, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, on behalf of opposite party No. 1-bank stating Inter alia that opposite party No. 2 namely Fartex Fashion Wear Limited availed loan facility to the tune of Taka 3,70,00,000 (Taka Three Crore Seventy Lac) only from opposite party No. 1 when opposite party No. 3 mortgaged the disputed flat to opposite party No. 1 by Mortgage Deed No. 10608 dated 14-5-2007 who also executed and registered an Irrevocable General Power of Attorney being No. 10609 dated 14-5-2007 in favour of opposite party No. 1 against availing of such loan for opposite party No. 2. As the borrower, opposite party No. 2 failed to repay the loan amount, opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff then instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 194 of 2012 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka and got a decree ex parte. Thereafter, opposite party No. 1 filed Artha Execution Case No. 1386 of 2019 before the same Court on the basis of the said decree. It has further been stated that, the opposite party No. 1 also initiated a Complaint Case being CR Case No. 469 of 2020 on 11-11-2020 under Sections 417/ 467/47/406/420/409/34 of the Penal Code, 1860 against the applicant and her vendor, Amena Islam (opposite party No. 3). Upon investigation of the case, the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) submitted Final Report discharging the applicant and submitted Charge Sheet against the applicant's vendor Amena Islam (opposite party No. 3) and opposite party No. 4. On the other hand, the applicant also filed a complaint case being CR Case No. 2784 of 2020 on 31-12-2020 under Sections 420/406/ 467/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860 against the opposite party No. 3 and her daughter, Abeda Islam and PBI submitted Charge Sheet against the opposite party No. 3 who also found involvement of one, Md. Saiful Alam, Assistant Director, Estate and Land-1, RAJUK, in the matter. 

4. However, the applicant came to know that Artha Rin Suit No. 194 of 2012 was decreed ex parte on 29-8-2019 and a decree was drawn on 5-9-2019 and pursuant to the said decree, opposite party No. 1 filed Artha Execution Case No. 1386 of 2019 (later renumbered as Artha Execution Case No. 156 of 2024) before the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka. The applicant also came to know that the executing Court vide Order No. 6 dated 2-11-2020 fixed the date of auction of the mortgaged properties to be held on 20-1-2021 by publishing auction notice in the 'Daily Amader Shomoy' and the 'Daily Samakal' on 14-12-2020 inviting bids from interested purchaser. The applicant finding no other alternative then filed Miscellaneous Case No. 04 of 2021 (later renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 06 of 2024) before the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka, under section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 read with Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 praying for releasing the disputed flat from auction sale. Upon hearing, the learned Advocates for the applicant and the opposite party No. 1, bank, the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka, initially vide order dated 11-2-2021 stayed the auction of the disputed flat. 

5. The respondent No. 1 as opposite party No. 1 contested the Miscellaneous Case by filing a written objection denying all the material statements so made in the application contending inter alia that the application is not maintainable, which is liable to be rejected. 

6. In order to dispose of the Miscellaneous case, the learned Judge of the trial court framed 02(two) distinct issues and the applicant examined 02(two) witnesses in support of her case while the opposite parties examined 01(one) witness. Apart from that, the petitioner produced several documents which were marked as exhibit nos. '1-15' series while the opposite parties also produced some documents which were marked as exhibit nos. '1-3 series'. 

7. Upon hearing the parties and due considering the materials and evidence on record, the learned Judge dismissed the Miscellaneous Case on contest against opposite party No. 1 by impugned judgment and order dated 28-10-2024. 

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order dated 28-10-2024 passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 06 of 2024, the applicant as appellant preferred this appeal. 

9. At the time of admission of the appeal, the appellant as petitioner filed an application for stay of the operation of the impugned judgment and order dated 28-10-2024 and this court vide order dated 15-12-2024 issued Rule and stayed the operation of the impugned judgment and order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.06 of 2024 for a period of 06(six) months which was lastly extended on 1-6-2025 for 3(three) months. 

10. Mr. Md. Awsafur Rahman along with Mr. Eeshith Monzul Shohiny, the learned counsels appearing on behalf of the appellant upon taking us to the impugned judgment and order, Memorandum of Appeal and application for stay at the outset submits that, the learned judge erred in law in failing to consider the case of the applicant in its proper perspective and had the case of the applicant considered, the impugned judgment and order would have been otherwise. To supplement the said submission, the learned counsel further submits that the Court did not proceed to examine or investigate the claim and objection raised by the applicant and no enquiry was made and thereby committed a grave illegality and hence the impugned judgment and order suffers from infirmity.  

11. The learned counsel further contends that the foundation of Artha Rin Suit No. 194 of 2012 was based on fraudulent activities allegedly committed by respondent No. 3 in collusion with respondent No. 1 and therefore the respondent No. 1 thus cannot reap the benefits out of such fraud, in view of the established legal maxim that "fraud vitiates all judicial proceedings" as held by the Appellate Division in the case of Government of Bangladesh and another vs Mashiur Rahman and others reported in 50 DLR (AD) 205. 

12. He next contends that the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka, while passing the impugned Judgment and Order dated 28-10-2024 disregarded the fact that the disputed property being a leasehold property, sale permission was obtained from the original Lessor i.e. the Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (RAJUK) prior to purchase. 

13. The learned counsel next submits that the disputed property is the only homestead of the appellant and in purchasing the disputed flat, the appellant and her husband exhausted all their personal savings and also borrowed a large amount of money from their close relatives and by committing fraud the respondent nos. 1 and 3 has put the appellant in extremely vulnerable and precarious position, which was not properly appreciated by the Court below rendering the impugned judgment and order unsustainable in law. 

14. In the same vein, Mr. AKM Ashiful Haque, the learned counsel contends that, the respondent No. 3 obtained permission from RAJUK to mortgage the suit property to respondent No. 1 for a home renovation loan but fact remains the respondent No. 1 disbursed a commercial loan and thereby committing a serious fraud but the learned judge failed to evaluate this aspect and thus most erroneously passed the impugned judgment and order which is liable to be set aside. 

15. In support of his contention, the learned counsel has referred to the decisions passed in the cases of Md. Sekandar and another vs Janata Bank and others, reported in 9 ALR (AD) 81 : 22 BLC (AD) 53, National Bank Limited and another vs MR Trading Company and others, reported in 72 DLR (2020) 1, Grindlays Bank Ltd vs Murree Brewery Company Ltd and another, reported in PLD 1954 Lahore 745, Ram Chandra Singh vs Savitri Devi and others, reported in (2003) 8 SCC 319. With these submissions and relying on these decisions, the learned counsel finally prays for allowing the appeal by setting aside the impugned judgment and order and making the Rule absolute. 

16. Per contra, Mr. Monjur Elahi Porag, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent-opposite party No. 1 by filing a counter-affidavit, very robustly opposes the contention taken by the learned senior counsel for the appellant and contends that the applicant-appellant's allegation that RAJUK was unaware of the mortgage of the disputed property in favour of the opposite party No. 1-bank has not been substantiated by any document where RAJUK has not denied of taking mortgage of the disputed flat and thus mere allegation of fraud unsupported by evidence cannot stand in the eye of law. He further submits that the opposite party No. 1-bank did not commit any fraud in obtaining the decree from the Artha Rin Adalat nor by publishing auction notice by filing execution case to sell the mortgaged property and the Artha Rin Adalat by considering the evidence rightly rejected the Miscellaneous Case. 

17. The learned Advocate further contends that if the applicant-appellant feels aggrieved by the conduct of opposite party No. 3-judgment-debtor, she may initiate independent legal proceedings against her and RAJUK and may claim appropriate compensation from them but she is not entitled to any remedy out of the Miscellaneous Case. He further contends that whether the loan disbursed to the judgment-debtor No. 3 for commercial or residential purpose and whether the mortgagor committed fraud in taking permission from RAJUK are all immaterial in adjudicating the Miscellaneous Case filed under section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

18. The learned counsel submits that the deed of mortgage was executed on 14.5-2007 in favour of the respondent No. 1 and after a lapse of 13 years, the opposite party No. 3 sold the self same flat to the appellant on 2-9-2020 depriving the opposite party No. 1-bank from realising its decreetal dues where there is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment and order which is liable to be sustained. With these submissions, the learned counsel prays for dismissing the appeal by affirming the impugned judgment and order and discharging the Rule. 

19. We have carefully considered the submissions advanced by the learned counsels for both the parties, perused the memorandum of appeal, counter-affidavit, impugned judgment and order and other materials on record. 

20. It is undisputed that respondent-opposite party No. 2 namely, M/s. Fartex Fashion wear Ltd. availed loan facilities of Taka 3,70,00,000 from opposite party no.1, namely National Credit and Commerce Bank Ltd. by mortgaging the suit flat along with other properties. Opposite party No.3, Mrs. Amena Islam mortgaged the suit flat to opposite party No.1 through Mortgage Deed No. 10608 on 14-5-2007 as a collateral of the said loan. But as the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 failed to repay the loan, the bank instituted Artha Rin Suit and the Artha Rin Adalat decreed the suit ex parte. But since the judgment-debtor failed to repay the decreetal amount to the bank as decree holder filed the Artha Execution Case. Meanwhile, the appellant as third party to the execution case filed the Miscellaneous Case. However, the execution Court passed the impugned judgment and order on 28-10-2024 dismissing the case refusing to release the suit flat. 

21. On going through the impugned judgment and order, we find that the claimant-applicant examined as many as two witnesses in support of her case and produced several documents which were marked as exhibit nos. '1-15' series and opposite party-respondent No.1 also examined one witness and produced documents in support of their case. After considering the submission advanced by the petitioner to the Miscellaneous Case, the Artha Rin Adalat passed the impugned judgment and order whicli we find to be reasonable. 

22. Further, the evidence of Mr. Sheikh Awshafur Rahman, appeared as PW 1 reveals that no search was conducted by the appellant before the concerned sub-registry office before purchasing the suit property as in his cross-examination, he asserted that" তফসিল বর্ণিত ভূমি | ক্রয়ের সময় বন্ধকী দলিল বিষয়ে জানতাম না। নালিশী জমি ক্রয়ের পূর্বে সাব রেজিঃ অফিসে তল্লাশি করি নাই। দরকার ছিল না।" But the appellant as purchaser of the suit flat was responsible to verify the genuineness and non-encumbrance of the suit flat to ascertain whether the transferor, Amena Islam has valid title and ownership over the suit flat. 

23. It appears from the record that the Mortgage Deed No. 10608 was executed by the respondent No. 3 in favour of respondent No. 1 on 14-5-2007 whereas the sale deed in favour of the appellant was executed on 2-9-2020 that is, after a lapse of 13 years. It is a settled principle that an earlier deed will take precedence over a subsequent deed. It is decided by this Court in fainullah and another vs Anu Mia and others, reported in 15 DLR 77 that in case of successive transfers of the self same property in favour of different persons by a common vendor by registered documents, the dispute as to the precedence of one document over the other has to be determined in accordance with the principles laid down in section 47 of the Registration Act. Thus the subsequent deed dated 2-9-2020 is hit by the provision laid down in section 47 of the Registration Act. 

24. It is claimed by the appellant that the respondent-opposite party No. 3 obtained permission from RAJUK to mortgage the property to respondent No. 1 for the purpose of a house renovation loan, but the bank disbursed a commercial loan and thereby the opposite party No. 3 in collusion with the opposite party No. 1-bank committed a serious fraud. In reply, the learned Advocate for the opposite party-respondent No. 1 submits that whether the loan disbursed was commercial or residential and whether the permission given by RAJUK was for renovation of home loan are immaterial in the context of loan recovery proceedings under the Artha Rin Suit as well as Artha Execution Case which is not matters to be determined in a Miscellaneous case filed under section 32 of Act. We find substance in the submission made by the learned Advocate for respondent No. 1-bank. The applicant-appellant being a subsequent transferee is not entitled to take advantage of the fraud alleged to have committed between opposite party nos. 1 and 3. 

25. On top of that since the suit flat was earlier mortgaged with respondent No. 1 by the respondent No. 3 and respondent No. 1 got a decree so there is no legal impediment to sell the mortgaged flat in execution case through auction and for the obvious reason, the appellant is not entitled to have the suit flat released. 

26. We find no illegality or perversity in the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned judge of the Artha Rin Adalat. The appellant has failed to prove her claim under section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. 

27. Given the above facts and circum-stances, we do not find any iota of illegality in the judgment and order passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 06 of 2024. We also find no merit or substance in the appeal and the Rule. 

28. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed, however without any order as to costs. 

29. The judgment and order dated 28-10-2024 passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No.06 of 2024 is hereby affirmed. 

30. Since the appeal is dismissed, the connected Rule being Civil Rule No. 735(FM) of 2024, is thus discharged. 

31. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands recalled and vacated. 

Let a copy of this judgment and order along with the lower courts record be communicated to the Court concerned forthwith. 

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Ashfaqur Rahman, Advocate with Mr. Santosh Kumar Sarker, Advocate -------- For the Petitioner
No one appears -------- For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Md. Shahidul Islam -------- Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Abu Taher -------- Opposite-Party
full_judgment:
In this revision Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 08.11.2020 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Rangpur in Other Appeal No. 70 of 2019 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.05.2019 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Rangpur in Other Suit No. 277 of 2013 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioners, as plaintiff, filed Other Suit No. 277 of 2013 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Rangpur for recovery of khas possession of 0.02 acre of land from the defendant demolishing illegal structure erected thereon.

3. The suit jote measuring 0.89 acre of land originally belonged to Bashiruddin, his name duly recorded in the last S.A. khatian. Bashiruddin died leaving behind wife Sahejannessa, five sons Farizuddin, Shamsul Hoque, Abu Taher, Abdul Bari the defendant in suit Md. Shahidul Islam, the plaintiff in suit and three daughters Mehera Khatun, Abeda Khatun and Rasheda Khatun.

4. Bashiruddin had other properties which were under amicable possession of the co-sharers. The daughters of Bashuiruddin relinquished their share in favour of their brothers in the suit jote. Sahezannessa by a registered deed of Heba-bil-Ewaj No. 13022 dated 11.07.1987 gifted her share to the plaintiffs. Five sons equally partitioned the rest land of the suit khatian and accordingly, each son got 0.1550 acre of land. The defendant by a registered sale deed No. 5477 dated 20.04.1991 sold 0.03 acre of land to one Mahmuda Khatun and thereafter by a registered sale deed dated 01.03.1998 bearing No. 2581 sold 0.0925 acre of land to Mosammat Sahera Khatun. The defendant further along with his other brothers and some of their heirs by a registered deed of exchange dated 25.09.1980 bearing No. 26632 transferred 0.17 acre of land to plaintiff and by virtue of the said deed the defendant transferred 0.0425 acre of land to the plaintiff.

5. As per amicable family partition three sisters got 0.27 acre of land out of 0.38 acre of Plot No. 2795 appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 1100 corresponding S.A. khatian No. 1005 and in the said khatian Abdul Bari got the rest 0.11 acre which he sold to one Matiar Rahman by a registered deed dated 04.09.1980. So far as the land measuring 1.35 acres of Plot No. 2718 appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 431/7 corresponding S.A khatian No. 441 is concerned the original owner Bashiruddin during his lifetime by a registered deed of sale dated 14.08.1972 bearing No. 28853 transferred 0.48 acre land and while in possession of the rest 0.87 acre died leaving behind wife Sahezannessa who got 0.1087 acre, five sons got 0.1175 acre each and three daughters got 0.0575 acre each. Three brothers namely Fariz, Shamsul alias Shamsher and Abdul Bari by a registered deed of sale dated 08.03.1979 bearing No. 8066 sold 0.51 acre to the defendant. By virtue of the said deed, the defendant actually got 0.0325 acre of land since the aforesaid three brothers sold excess to their admitted share. The defendant sold 0.72 acre of land, in excess to his admitted share to one Abdul Khaleque Siddique by a registered Sale deed dated 12.07.1980 bearing No. 22025.

6. The defendant transferred his entire share in all ejmal khatians and being titless in the paternal properties in the aforementioned manner shifted to Hazarihat with his family and started living there permanently. After a long time he decided to live with close proximity of his paternal property. For the purpose of erecting house and requested the plaintiff to allow him to erect two chala ghar adjacent to plaintiff’s house and accordingly, the plaintiff accorded permission to defendant to erect chala ghar on 0.02 acre of land which is a part of the plaintiff’s residential house, temporarily. After two years the plaintiff when in his need of the said land requested the defendant to vacate and surrender the land, the defendant refused. Lastly, on 15.11.2013, the plaintiff finally demanded vacant possession of the land but the defendant denied to do so, and hence, the plaintiff filed the present suit for recovery of khas possession of 0.02 acre of land demolishing the structure erected thereon.

7. The defendant filed written statement but did not file any documents in support of his written statement. The learned trial Court by an Order dated 13.05.2019 rejected the written statement as the same was not accompanied with documents, and the learned trial court on the same date took up the suit for ex parte disposal. Plaintiff as PW1 deposed in support of his case and submitted documents in support of his case which was marked as exhibit Nos. 1, 2 and 3, but the learned trial court by a judgment and decree dated 13.05.2019 (decree signed on 19.05.2019) dismissed the suit ex parte treating the suit filed under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act with an observation that removal of structure was not permissible under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, inasmuch as, the plaintiff was not dispossessed by the defendant.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the petitioner filed Title Appeal No. 70 of 2019 before the District Judge, Rangpur which was subsequently transferred to the court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Rangpur for hearing and disposal, who after hearing by its impugned judgment and decree dated 08.11.2020 dismissed the appeal and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court. At this juncture, the petitioners moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

9. Mr. Ashfaqur Rahman with Mr. Santosh Kumar Sarker, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submit that the petitioner filed the suit for a decree of recovery of possession and nowhere in the plaint, the plaintiff stated and taken recourse to Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, paying half the advalorem court fees, but the trial court on its own motion came to a conclusion that the suit has been filed by the plaintiff is under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, which does not permit the plaintiff to seek recovery of possession by removal of structure raised by the defendant on the suit property.

10. He submits that, the trial court cannot treat the suit under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act on its own motion. He candidly argued that the trial court if finds that without declaration of title the prayer as made is not maintainable, the plaintiff would have got an opportunity to amend the plaint before the appellate court.

11. He argued that against the judgment and decree of the trial court in a suit under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, revision shall lie not appeal. In the instant case the plaintiff preferred appeal and the appeal was also dismissed not on the ground of non-maintainability, but dismissed by the appellate court concurring with the findings of the trial court that the suit is under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act. However, he submits that, to avoid complication and confusion and to get the suit disposed of properly by the trial court, the petitioner filed an application praying for amendment of the plaint by way of incorporation of a prayer in respect of title of the plaintiff in the suit property which was allowed by this Court on 11.11.2025. Therefore, he prays for sending the suit on remand to the trial court for fresh trial by setting aside the judgment and decree of both the courts below. None appears for the opposite parties to oppose the rule. Heard the learned Advocates for the petitioner, have gone through the revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, plaint in suit, written statement, evidence both oral and documentary and impugned judgment and order of both the courts below. From perusal of record in particular plaint in suit, it appears that the suit was filed by the plaintiff for a decree of recovery of possession and the plaint did not mention under which provision of law it was filed. The plaintiff, for the prayer made in the plaint paid advalorem court fees on the basis of valuation of the suit. The defendant though appeared and filed written statement ultimately the written statement was struck off by the trial court on the ground that the defendant did not file any document in support of his written statement. The defendant did not agitate the order before any higher court, meaning thereby, he conceded correctness of the order. The defendant refrained from contesting the suit, however, the trial court took the matter for hearing ex parte. The plaintiff deposed himself and submitted some documents in support of his claim. The trial court by its judgment and decree dated 13.05.2019 dismissed the suit ex parte holding that this is a suit under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, it does not permit removal of structure by the defendant on the suit land. In appeal, the appellate court also concurred with the findings and observations of the trial court and finally concluded that the suit is not maintainable under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act. It is true that judgment and decree passed by the trial court in a suit for recovery of possession under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act is not appealable, but revisable before this Court. In the instant case while the plaintiff preferred appeal before the appellate court, learned District Judge did not address that point, rather dealt with the appeal on merit and finally decided that under provision of Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, removal of structure by the defendant on the property not allowed and on that ground the appeal was dismissed affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court.

12. The petitioner feeling necessary to get the plaint amended only by incorporation of a prayer for declaration of title, filed an application and got the plaint amended, added the said prayer for declaration of title. From plain reading of the plaint, it appears that the statements made by the plaintiff indicates that the suit was not filed under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, but it was filed under Sections 42 and 8 of the Specific Relief Act, but the learned Advocate for the plaintiff failed to make prayer to the effect that the plaintiff has title in the suit property. Because of incorporation of such prayer, I think that a fresh trial of the suit is necessary affording an opportunity to the plaintiff to prove his case by adducing sufficient evidence to secure ends of justice. Therefore, I think that the purpose of the plaintiff will serve and justice will be met, if the suit is sent back on remand to the trial court for fresh trial affording opportunity to the parties to adduce evidence and to pass a judgment a fresh by the trial court.

13. In view of the above, I find merit in the rule as well as in the submissions of the leaned Advocate for the petitioner.

14. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however, without any order as to costs.

15. Judgment and decree of both the courts below are hereby set aside. The suit is sent back on remand to the trial court for fresh trial affording opportunity to the parties to adduce evidence to prove their case within shortest possible time preferably within 06 (six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order positively.

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned and send down the lower court records at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Md. Bakhtiar Hossain, Advocate ----For the Defendant -Appellant-Petitioner.
Mr. Ashfaqur Rahman, Advocate ----For the Plaintiffs-Defendant-Opposite Parties.
parties:
Md. Khairul Islam Lebu. ----Defendant -Appellant-Petitioner.
Vs.
Mrs. Rupali Akter Rupa and another. ---- Plaintiffs-Defendant-Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
Md. Toufiq Inam, J. This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 31.05.2022 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Court No. 3, Rangpur, in Family Appeal No. 39 of 2021, affirming the order dated 28.03.2021 passed by the learned Family Court, Pirgonj, Rangpur, in Family Execution Case No. 08 of 2016, rejecting the petitioner‟s application filed in the execution proceeding to consider the fact of talak/divorce, should not be set aside and/or why such other or further order or orders should not be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The opposite party, as wife, instituted Family Suit No. 83 of 2013 before the learned Family Court, Pirgonj, Rangpur, claiming dower and maintenance from the present petitioner, her husband. Upon full trial, the Family Court partly decreed the suit directing the husband to pay specified amounts of dower, arrear maintenance, and continuing maintenance. The husband did not prefer any appeal against the decree, and thus it attained finality.

3. Subsequently, the decree-holder wife filed Family Execution Case No. 08 of 2016 for realization of the decretal dues. During pendency of the execution proceeding, the judgment-debtor husband filed an application dated 06.02.2020, producing a talaqnama (divorce document) asserting that he had divorced his wife earlier but could not produce the document during trial. He prayed that, in view of the divorce, the maintenance component of the decree be modified and the continuing maintenance be exempted.

4. Upon hearing, the learned Family Execution Court, by order dated 28.03.2021, rejected the application holding that since the issue of divorce had already been raised and not proved at trial, there was no scope to adjudicate the matter at the execution stage.

5. Aggrieved, the husband preferred Family Appeal No. 39 of 2021, against the Family Execution Court‟s aforesaid order dated 28.03.2021, which was dismissed on 31.05.2022 by the learned Joint District Judge, Court No. 3, Rangpur, affirming the order of the Family Court. Hence, the husband has moved this revisional application and obtained the present Rule

6. Mr. Md. Bakhtiar Hossain, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the Family Court, being vested with “all powers of a Civil Court” under section 16(3A) of the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985, is competent to consider relevant additional evidence during execution. He argues that the divorce was not a subsequent event but a pre-existing fact pleaded in the written statement, and that the talaqnama now produced merely substantiates that earlier plea.

7. He further contends that under Muslim law, a divorced woman is not entitled to maintenance beyond the iddat period, and enforcing continuing maintenance after a valid divorce amount to unjust enrichment.

8. Placing reliance on Robiul Islam vs Shahanara Akhter, 77 DLR (HCD) 340, learned counsel submits that a Family Court exercising powers akin to a Civil Court may decide factual issues arising during execution when such determination is necessary for effective enforcement of the decree. Therefore, the executing Court ought to have received and considered the divorce document instead of rejecting the application on the ground of lack of jurisdiction.

9. Per contra, Mr. Ashfaqur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing with Mr. Sumit Kumar Sarker for the opposite party, submits that the decree in Family Suit No. 83 of 2013 has long attained finality and cannot be reopened in execution. The issue of divorce was raised and specifically decided at trial with a finding that “the defendant failed to prove the talaq.” Hence, the executing Court cannot vary, reopen, or revisit an adjudicated fact.

10. He contends that the talaqnama now produced, not having been proved during trial, cannot be accepted at the execution stage. The proper remedy of the petitioner was to prefer an appeal or seek review, not to seek modification in execution upon adducing additional evidence. He therefore prays for discharge of the Rule.

11. Upon hearing the learned Advocates and examining the record, it is evident that the decree in Family Suit No. 83 of 2013 has attained finality. The Family Court, while decreeing the suit, expressly considered the plea of talak and found that the defendant-husband failed to prove the alleged divorce. These finding forms part of the decree and cannot be disturbed collaterally.

12. Once a decree attains finality, the executing Court is duty-bound to execute it as it stands. It cannot reopen factual findings, reassess evidence, or modify substantive reliefs granted therein.

13. Under section 16(3A) of the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985, the Family Court is vested with the powers of a Civil Court in execution. These powers are procedural in nature- enabling the court to enforce the decree effectively, such as by summoning witnesses, taking accounts, attaching property, granting instalments, or recording satisfaction in accordance with procedure laid down in Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure. However, this authority does not extend to reopening adjudicated facts or altering the operative terms of the decree.

14. This Court has carefully considered the petitioner‟s reliance on Robiul Islam vs Shahanara Akhter, 77 DLR (HCD) 340. In that case, the judgment-debtor-husband in a Family Execution Case prayed to pay the decretal amount by instalments. During the ensuing Family Miscellaneous Appeal, he further prayed to adduce oral evidence to prove a talaqnama, marking it as an exhibit. The appellate court rejected that prayer, but the High Court Division in revision, interpreting section 16(3A) of the Ordinance, held that “Sub-section 3A of section 16 provides that the executing Court in a Family suit shall be vested with "all powers" of a court under the code. The language of the law providing for "all powers" under the code is plain and simple and easily understood.”

15. With profound respect, this Court finds it difficult to endorse such a broad interpretation of section 16(3A) of the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985 as enunciated in 77 DLR (HCD) 340. The said provision indeed empowers the Family Court, at the stage of execution, to exercise “all powers of a civil court” for the limited purpose of enforcement of a decree. However, the phrase “all powers” cannot be read in isolation to enlarge the jurisdiction of the executing Family Court beyond the scope of execution proceedings, nor can it import appellate or review powers such as those contemplated under Order XLI, Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure. To do so would render nugatory the well-settled principle that an executing court cannot go behind, vary, or modify the decree which it is bound to execute. The Family Execution Court is not an appellate or revisional forum; it cannot re-appraise evidence or admit new evidence to reopen findings already merged in the final decree.

16. The approach adopted in 77 DLR (HCD) 340, though well-intentioned to ensure complete justice, risks conferring quasi-appellate powers upon an executing court, thereby disturbing the finality of adjudication and blurring the jurisdictional distinction between „adjudication‟ and „execution‟. The legislative intent behind section 16(3A) is to make the Family Court self-contained for execution purposes, allowing it to employ procedural tools of the Code to ensure realization of its decree, but not to empower it to re-determine issues of fact or law already adjudicated.

17. It may therefore be observed that this Court‟s view does not amount to overruling the precedent of 77 DLR (HCD) 340 but rather distinguishes it on clear factual and legal grounds: while 77 DLR dealt with the power of a Family Execution Court to regulate the mode of satisfaction of a decree and to consider instalments in payment, the present case concerns a challenge to the subsistence of the decree itself by introducing a plea of divorce, an issue squarely adjudicated and concluded in the main suit.

18. In the present case, the petitioner does not seek procedural facilitation but a substantive variation of the decree itself by introducing a talaqnama to nullify continuing maintenance. This is beyond the jurisdiction of the executing Family Court.

19. This court is of the considered view that a Family Court, though vested with powers of a Civil Court under section 16(3A) of the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985, may exercise those powers only for the purpose of execution, adjustment, and enforcement of a decree, but cannot reopen, vary, or re-adjudicate any factual or legal issue already decided in the original suit. This principle preserves the doctrine of finality of judicial decisions and prevents executing courts from assuming appellate or review powers under the guise of procedural authority.

20. While the Family Court, in execution, may act with procedural flexibility similar to a Civil Court, it cannot transgress the boundary of the decree. To hold otherwise would frustrate execution proceedings, invite re-litigation, and erode judicial discipline. Both the courts below rightly held that there was no jurisdiction to consider the alleged divorce at the execution stage.

21. For the reasons discussed above, this Court finds no illegality, impropriety, or material irregularity in the impugned orders warranting interference under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

22. Accordingly, the Rule is discharged.

23. The interim order of stay stands vacated.

Let the copy of this judgment be sent to the courts below at once.

End.

lawyer:
AF Hasan Ariff with Ramzan Ali Sikder and Abdullah M Hasan Advocates-For the Petitioner.
SM Muniruzzaman, AAG-For the Respondents.
parties:
Unique Hotel and Resorts Limited ------ Petitioner 
Vs.
National Board of Revenue and others   ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J: On an application made by the petitioner under article 102 of the Constitution, a Rule Nisi was issued in the following terms:

"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the arbitrary and discriminatory refusal of exemption from payment of customs duties, VAT and other taxes pursuant to section 20 of the Customs Act, 1969 and section 14 of the VAT Act, 1991 against the importation of various capital machinery for setting up a five star hotel as contained in Nothi No. 2( 15) Shu: Mu (moukuf)/2000 dated 1-3-20005 (Annexure-A) and non-consideration of the petitioner's application dated 9-8-2006 (Annexure-P) and the assessment of duties and taxes at a higher rate as evident from the Bill of Entry No.C-16047 dated 20-8-2006 (Annexure-A-1) in disregard of the concessionary rate at 5% as contained in SRO No .114 dated 8-6-2006 should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and unconstitutional and void being violative of the fundamental rights of the petitioner guaranteed under Articles 27, 31, 40 and 42 of the Constitution and why the respondents should not be directed to grant exemptions to the petitioner in respect of the petitioner's imported capital machineries as per SRO No.114/2006 dated 8-6-2006 read with section 20 of the Customs Act, 1969 and section 14 of the VAT Act, 1991 or such other or further orders as to this court may seem fit and proper."

2. Material facts necessary for disposal of the rule, in brief, are as under:

The petitioner, Unique Hotel and Resorts Limited is a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1994. The petitioner has undertaken the construction work of a five star hotel of the highest international standard for catering the highest class of international client. The petitioner was incorporated as a joint venture company for implementation of a joint venture project for construction and running of a five star luxury hotel with Star wood Hotel and Resort Worldwide, a company incorporated in the United States of America, which owns and/or manages 750 luxury and high standard hotels in 70 countries under different names, such as, Westin, Sheraton and St. Regis.

3.In accordance with SRO No. 158-Law/2000/1839/Customs dated 8-6-2000 (hereinafter referred to as SRO 158) and pursuant to section 20 of the Customs Act, 1969 (the Act, in short) and section 14 of the মূল্য সংযোজন কর আইন, ১৯৯১ ( the VAT Act, in brief) the petitioner submitted an application dated 19-3-200 I along with a list of capital machineries praying for exemption of duties. taxes, etc. The respondent No.4, Second Secretary, Customs (Regulation and Budget), National Board of Revenue, Dhaka by his letter bearing Nothi No. 2(7) Customs Valuation (exemption)/2000/218 dated 17-4-2001 refused to grant exemption in respect of capital machineries for which petitioner sought for exemption without showing any reasons whatsoever. Thereafter, the petitioner applied to the Board of Investment (BOI, in short) on 10-6-2001 and 12-9-2001 requesting it to take necessary steps to grant exemption to the petitioner's project under the Board of Investment Act. After receipt of the application and the letter from the petitioner, BOl forwarded its recommendation by its letter bearing Memo No. B: Bo:/Ni &Sa-1/2607/200 I dated 12-9-2001 to the respondent No.1 and requested the Chairman, National Board of Revenue ( in short, NBR) to take necessary steps for granting exemption to the petitioner for proper implementation of the petitioner's project. After forwarding of the recommendation by Bol, the petitioner submitted another application on 24-9-2001 before NBR along with a list of machineries in respect of which exemption had been sought. But without any response. Then the petitioner wrote another letter on 1-11-2001 to Bol seeking confirmation that the Hotel and Tourism Sector has been declared as an industrial thrust sector and therefore, entitled to the exemption in respect of capital machineries as per Bol Guidelines for Investment in Bangladesh. Then Bol by its letter bearing No. BoI/R&I/260/2001/1265 dated 6-11-2001 confirmed that the petitioner's project is entitled to the facilities in respect of import of capital machineries. The respondent No.4 again refused to grant exemption to the petitioner. Then the petitioner filed another application dated 1-12-2001 praying for exemption by endorsing letter dated 6-11-2001 issued by Bol. But without any response. Thereafter, the petitioner wrote another letter dated 15-4-2002 praying for exemption on the machineries and goods with the application dated 1-12-2001 and then the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 by an order dated 9-5-2002 granted exemptions on certain machineries. Thereafter, they added some other items with it. Subsequently, being aggrieved by the respondents' refusal to grant exemption with regard to all the capital machineries, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 2861 of 2004 and a rule was issued in that writ petition and subsequently, the capital machineries were released pursuance to an ad-interim order of the High Court Division subject to some conditions.

4. Another applicant M/s Sarina Inn Limited, Dhaka (the Sarina, in brief) applied for similar exemption for setting up its hotel project. The respondents granted exemption to the Sarina in respect of much wider categories of articles by an order dated 6-5-2002. The petitioner has as many as seven applications during 20-7-2002 to 15-12- 2005 but without any success. Finally, the petitioner submitted an application before the Minister, Ministry of Finance and Planning on 6-1-2005 seeking exemption under section 20 of the Customs Act and section 14 of the VAT Act, but without result. The petitioner imported electrical refrigerators under Letter of Credit No. 0746-0601-0122 dated 4-6-2006 issued by the City Bank Limited, Kawran Bazar Branch, Dhaka. The respondents have granted exemption in terms of SRO 158 and section 20 of the Act and section 14 of the VAT Act in favour of the Sarina by an order dated 6-5-2002, Sea Gull Hotels Limited by an order dated 3-5-2001, M/s Nandan Park Limited by order dated 14-12-2002, M/s. Bashundhara City, Abul Khair Steel Products and Shah Cement Industries Limited. But till date the petitioner did not get any response. The impugned order of refusal, assessment of customs duties and taxes treating the goods as commercial imports instead of concessionary rate on the capital machineries imported, non-consideration of the petitioner's application and failure to release of the petitioner's goods at concessionary rate of 5% in terms of SRO No. 114/Ain/2006/2106/Shalko dated 8-6-2006 (SRO 114) are without lawful authority.

5. In this backdrop the petitioner has filed this writ petition and obtained rule with an order of release of the goods on paying of 50% of duties and taxes in cash and rest duties and taxes on furnishing bank guarantee.

6. Respondent No.1 i.e. NBR contested the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the statements made in the writ petition contending inter alia, that the Government under section 20 of the Customs Act may allow full or partial exemption from statutory duties on goods under certain circumstances. Such exemption does not create any vested right in favour of the importers. Assessment of customs duties at the enhanced rate was not illegal on 1-12-2001. Respondent Nos. 3 and 4 by an order dated 9-5-2002 granted exemption of duties and taxes on certain machineries of the petitioner. Subsequently, that exemption order was .revised on 19-10-2004 and some other machineries were included in it. Respondent No.2 refused to give exemption from payment of duties and taxes in favour of the Sena Hotel Developments Limited by an order dated 14-12-2004 and others. Since the petitioner has been enjoying partial benefit from exemption of payment of duties and taxes on certain articles/machineries it cannot claim for further benefit on the basis of the same recommendation which has already been acted upon. The Government has a power to grant exemption which can be partial or whole subject to certain conditions. No importers can claim absolute exemption as of right. The petitioner filed an application for concessional rate of duties on imported machineries and others which do not fall under SRO No. 158 and or SRO 114. Since the petitioner's items are not included in these SROs and it is not legally entitled to get the benefit of SRO No.158 or SRO No.114 as of right. This writ petition is misconceived, not maintainable and, as such, the rule is liable to be discharged.

7. The petitioner has filed a supplementary affidavit and an affidavit-in-reply stating that the power to grant exemption under section 20 of the Customs Act from payment of customs duties is not completely unfettered. The Government must, at all material times exercise the said power by rational, non-discriminatory standard or norm and if the Government departs from such standard or norm in any particular case or cases, the action of the Government would be liable to be struck down on ground of being arbitrary, unreasonable and discriminatory and, as such, the rule is liable to be made absolute.

8. Mr AF Hasan Ariff, the learned Advocate for the petitioner appearing with Mr Ramzan Ali Sikder and Mr Abdullah M Hasan has taken us through the writ petition and the materials on record and advanced the following arguments:

(i) From annexure-J of the affidavit-in- opposition, it transpires that as per direction of the Minister the prayer for exemption of the petitioner's goods from payment of duties, taxes, etc. was not considered, but the Minister has no jurisdiction to interfere with the power of NBR;

(ii) as refusal was made at the direction of the Minister, the impugned order of refusal is without lawful authority;

(iii) the Sarina, Sea Gull Hotels Limited, M/s. Nandan Park Limited, M/s Bashundhara City, Abul Khair Products and Shah Cement Industries Ltd. were granted exemption in terms of SRO 158 and under section 20 of the Customs Act and under section 14 of the VAT Act;

(iv) in the petitioner's case only partial exemption was allowed and therefore, the partial exemption granted to the petitioner is arbitrary and discriminatory and the petitioner is entitled to get exemption for its capital machineries;

(v) under section 20 of the Customs Act and under section 14 of the VAT Act the power of the Government and NBR respectively are not unfettered and it must be exercised reasonably;

(vi) BOI directed NBR to grant exemption and therefore, there is no scope whatsoever for refusal by NBR as the order of BOI is to be treated as decision of the Government and in such view of the mailer the petitioner is entitled to get exemption and, as such, the rule is liable to be made absolute.

9. In support of his arguments, the learned Advocates for the petitioner relies on the decisions of the following cases:

(i) The Chairman, National Board of Revenue vs Beximco Infusions Ltd. Dhaka, reported in 17 BLD (AD) 83 = 51 DLR (AD) 36;

(ii) Bharat Heavy Electrical Ltd. vs M Chandrasekhar Reddy, reported in 2 Supreme Court Cases, 2008, 481;

(iii) Authorized Officer, DIT, Dhaka vs AW Mallik, reported in 20 DLR (SC) 229 ;

(iv) Sterling Computers Ltd. Vs Mis. M &N Publication Limited, reported in AIR 1996 (SC) 51.

10. In reply, Mr SM Muniruzzaman, the learned Assistant Attorney General submits that this writ petition so far as it relates to assessment of duties and taxes as per the existing law on the bill of entry No. C-16047 dated 20-8-2006 is not maintainable inasmuch as the goods are imported under PS 1 scheme and according to CRF certificate the goods were assessed to duties and taxes and therefore, if the petitioner is aggrieved by said assessment order, the proper relief is by way of filing an application before the review committee and not in writ jurisdiction. He next submits that the power to exempt the customs duties is under section 20 of the Customs Act and therefore, the Chairman of NBR has no authority to exempt the customs duties and the petitioner not having applied to the Government for exemption of customs duties under section 20 of the Customs Act refusal to exempt the customs duties are absolutely lawful. He further contends that under section 20 of the Customs Act, Government has discretionary power of exemption from payment of duties on any goods under certain conditions only. He further submits that the Government and NBR are to consider exemption on each goods subject to certain terms and conditions in exercise of its discretionary power. He next submits that admittedly the petitioner has been enjoying the exemption of duties and taxes on certain capital machineries and subsequently, by letter dated 19- 10-2004 NBR extended exemption from duties and taxes on certain items. He also submits that in other cases also the NBR Government did not allow exemption from duties and taxes as a whole but partial and also refused exemption such as, Sena Hotel Developments Ltd. (Radisson), Sea Gull Ltd. He further submits that discretionary power has been used by NBR reasonably and not arbitrarily or discriminately. He also submits that the decision of Bol is not binding upon NBR inasmuch as it is the (Government who is to exempt the customs duties and taxes under the Customs Act and NBR is the authority under section 14 of the VAT Act to exempt VAT and supplementary duty. He next submits that NBR is not bound to comply with the direction of Bol and Bol also did not give any specific directions in its order but only forwarded a letter. He lastly submits that this writ petition is misconceived, not tenable in law, not maintainable and the rule is liable to be discharged.

11. In support of his contentions, the learned Assistant Attorney-General has referred to the unreported judgment dated 4-6-2001 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 344 and 345 of 1995 (Beximco Engineering Ltd. vs The Chairman, National Board of Revenue) and unreported judgment dated 17-5-2010 passed in Writ Petition No. 8110. of 2009 (Jamuna Television Ltd vs National Board of Revenue).

12. We have examined the writ petition, the affidavit-in-opposition, the supplementary affidavit, the affidavit-in-reply filed by the petitioner and the connected materials on record. We have also considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the contending parties and the decisions as referred to the learned Advocates of both sides.

13. It is not disputed that the petitioner has undertaken the construction work of a five star hotel of the highest international standard. It is not also denied that the petitioner for importation of the capital machineries for setting up of its hotel applied to the Chairman, NBR for exemption from payment of customs duties, VAT and supplementary duties in terms of SRO No. 158 and under section 20 of the Customs Act as well as under section 14 of the VAT Act. Admittedly, the petitioner earlier filed an application for exemption of duties and taxes before NBR which was refused and the petitioner then obtained certificate from Bol and NBR after several communications eventually allowed exemption from duties and taxes in respect of certain machineries included in its order. Admittedly, subsequently NBR by letter dated 19-10-200 extended exemption of some items to the petitioner. Further the petitioner imported some electrical refrigerators and submitted bill of entry No.C/1607 dated 20-8-2006 (Annexure A-1 to the writ petition).

14. It transpires from the materials on record (Annexure-P to the Writ Petition) that the Managing Director of the petitioner applied to NBR for release of the imported machineries under bill of entry No. C/1607 dated 20-8-2006 without payment of duties and taxes for construction of hotel. The petitioner failed to produce any letter showing that it was refused by NBR but photostat copy of the note sheet of NBR has been annexed to the writ petition. The photostat copy is not legible. However, it appears from the typed copy that exemption from the duties and taxes for 5 items were allowed to the petitioner and it was admittedly extended for certain other items. The petitioner applied for importation of other materials with the same facilities and the Chairman wrote in the note "may regret" and NBR decided to inform it to the petitioner. However, it is not disputed that NBR refused to) exempt the duties and taxes at concession rate of 5% in terms of SRO No. 114 and pursuant 10 section 20 of the Customs Act and also section 14 of the VAT Act.

15. The petitioner claims that refusal was done at the instruction of the Minister who had no jurisdiction to pass such order. The petitioner earlier accepted partial exemption and extension of exemption on some items without taking any legal steps.

16. In this connection the photocopy of the order dated 3-12-2003 may be looked into.

17. In note No.73 dated 3-12-2003 (annexure-3 to the affidavit-in-opposition) it was stated that the Minister earlier approved exemption permission to the petitioner and the Sarina on 24-4-2004 and 25-3-2003. However, the Minister subsequently refused to approve similar proposal on 12-9-2002 and 25-3-2003.This writ petition is not over challenging the said order. In the instant case, the petitioner filed another application for exemption of other machineries with the same benefit as has been granted to it earlier relating to some other capital machineries and from Annexure-A to the writ petition it transpires that Board refused the same on 16-2-2005 by note No. 154. Therefore, it cannot be presumed that due to a direction passed in the year 2003, the Board refused to consider the application of the petitioner in the year 2006 at the direction of the Minister. Moreover, there is no indication in the note that the refusal was made at the direction of the Minister. Furthermore, admittedly NBR by letter dated 19-10-2004 extended its exemption to the petitioner on some additional items which is after the order of the Minister. Therefore, there is no iota of evidence showing that the impugned refusal was made by NBR at the direction of the Minister.

18. Interestingly, the petitioner claimed that the Minister has no authority in this matter but in Paragraph 5(k) of the writ petition, the petitioner himself stated that the petitioner finally submitted an application before the Minister on 6-1-2005 seeking exemption. In one hand, the petitioner claimed that the Minister has no authority to deal with this matter, on the other hand, it seems that the petitioner applied to the Minister for the such exemption.

19. Be that as it may, in view of the discussions made above, we are of the opinion that the impugned refusal was not made at the instruction/direction of the Minister.

20. As it is held that refusal of NBR was not at the direction of the Minister, the decisions as referred to by the learned Advocate on this question needs no discussions.

21. Now let us come to the next question whether refusal to the petitioner from exemption of duties and taxes on certain items is unreasonable, arbitrary and discriminatory.

22. It appears from the affidavit-in-opposition that Bol issued a letter to the Chairman, NBR

"উপযুক্ত বিষয়ে মেসার্স সারিনা ইন লিঃ এর নিকট হতে প্রাপ্ত ২২-১-২০০২ তারিখে পত্রে তিন তারা হোটেল শিল্প প্রকল্পের জন্য আধুনিক স্থাপত্য শৈলীতে ২০ তলা বিশিষ্ট ভবন নির্মাণের জন্য প্রিফেব্রিকেটেড নির্মাণ সামগ্রী, আসবাবপত্র,যন্ত্রপাতি এবং অন্যান্য মালামাল আমদানির ক্ষেত্রে রেয়াতী হার কর প্রয়োগ করার জন্য আবেদন করেছেন (আবেদন পত্রের ফটোকপি সংযুক্ত)। শিল্প প্রতিষ্ঠানের কর্তৃপক্ষের বর্ণনামতে এ ধরনের স্থাপত্য কাজ দেশে এই প্রথম। এই সেবা শিল্প প্রতিষ্ঠানটি পর্যটন সেক্টরভুক্ত একটি বেসরকারি প্রতিষ্ঠান যা মোট আয়ের ৬০% বৈদেশিক মুদ্রা অর্জন করবে ও প্রায় ১০০লোকের কর্মসংস্থান সৃষ্টি করবে।

উক্ত প্রকল্পটি "পর্যটন" এর থ্রাস্ট সেক্টরের অন্তর্ভুক্ত একটি স্বীকৃত সেবা শিল্প। শিল্পনীতি ১৯৯৯ এর ৪.৯ ধারায় সরকার কর্তৃক থ্রাস্ট সেক্টরের শিল্পকে বিশেষ প্রণোদনা ও সহায়তা (Special incentives & Supportive Measures) প্রদান করা হবে বলে ঘোষণা করা হয়েছে। শিল্পনীতি ১৯৯৯ এর ৭.৮ ধারায় ঘোষণা করা হয়েছে "অগ্রাধিকার শিল্প খাত"(Trust Sector) হিসাবে চিহ্নিত

শিল্প এবং ক্ষুদ্র ও কুটির শিল্পের ক্ষেত্রে বিশেষ রাজস্ব সুবিধা প্রদান করা হইবে। এই স্ব খাতে সরকার মাঝে মাঝে আর্থিক সুবিধা প্রদানের ব্যবস্থা করিবে। এছাড়াও শিল্পনীতির ১০.৬  ধারায় ঘোষণা করা হয়েছে "সরকার অগ্রাধিকার প্রাপ্ত খাত (Trust Sector) হিসাবে চিহ্নিত রপ্তানিমুখী শিল্পখাতকে বিশেষ সুবিধা ও "ভেঞ্ছার ক্যাপিটাল" সুবিধা প্রদান করা হইবে।

আধুনিক স্থাপত্য শৈলী ব্যবহার নির্মিতব্য তিন তারা হোটেলে সেবা শিল্প প্রতিষ্ঠানটি থ্রাস্ট বিধায় সরকার ঘোষণা মতে প্রকল্পের জন্য আমদানিতব্য প্রিফেব্রিকেটেড নির্মাণ সামগ্রী, আসবাবপত্র, যন্ত্রপাতি এবং অন্যান্য মালামাল এর উপর সম্বাব্য সুযোগ প্রদান বিবেচনা করার জন্য নির্দেশক্রমে সুপারিশ করা হলো।"

23. On the basis of the said letter, said facilities were given to the Sarina by NBR by order dated 6-5-2002 (Annexure-4 to the affidavit-in-opposition).

24. It transpires from the order of NBR dated 3-5-2001 (Annexure M-l to the writ petition) that partial exemption of taxes and duties were allowed to Hotel Seagull Ltd. situated at Cox's Bazar on specified goods stating the reasons thereof and subject to certain terms and conditions. The machineries and parts, were also described in this order.

25. Therefore, the exemption given to Sea Gull Ltd. is not also for all goods/machineries but to certain goods which is also subject to certain terms and conditions.

26. From the application of Sena Development Ltd (Annexure-I) to the affidavit-in-opposition and office order dated 14-12-2004 passed by NBR (Annexure-2 to the affidavit-in-opposition), it transpires that NBR refused to consider the application for exemption of Sena Development Ltd. for construction of five star hotel, namely, Radison. Therefore, it is evident that for construction of another five star hotel NBR refused payer for some exemptions.

27. M/s Nandan Park Limited, M/s Bashundhara City, Abul Khair Products and Shah Cement Industries Ltd are not hotel business but different categories of industries and so, those are not in the same compartment as the petitioner. Thus, those cases need no discussions in this case.

<u>28. On going through the materials on record as discussed, we are of the view that NBR has decided the merit of each cases individually and exemption was not allowed to all hotels as a whole. Thus, it cannot be said that the order of refusal by NBR is unreasonable, discriminatory or arbitrary. Under section 20 of the Customs Act the Government and under section 14 of the VAT Act, NBR is empowered to exempt full or partial exemption from customs duties, VAT, etc. on any goods. Such power does not create any vested right in favour of all the importers.</u>

29. In view of the above, it cannot be said that the impugned order of refusal passed by NBR is unreasonable or arbitrary or discriminatory so as to interfere with it.

30. As from the materials on record it is found that the refusal is not discriminatory, we do not like to discuss the decisions as referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioner being redundant.

31. The last question to be decided in this rule is whether order passed by Bol is binding upon NBR.

32. On this question, the learned Advocates for the petitioner has referred to the decision reported in 17 BLD (AD) 83 = 51 DLR (AD) 36, Appellate Division have held as under:

" .....The scheme of the Act seems to be that decision of the Board of Investment relating, inter alia, to facilities for Implementation of a project in due time shall be implemented as a Government decision. Not only that, under section 11 (6) when the Board of Investment decides that the respondent should get the benefit of SRO dated 25-7-1990 it amounts to a decision of the National Board of Revenue itself which shall be implemented". This being the position in law and fact, we fail to see on what good reason and why the National Board of Revenue became so adamant. As for the non-issuance of a required certificate by the Board of Investment under the aforesaid SRO which was insisted by the National Board of Revenue, the former explained the technical difficulty in a subsequent letter to the National Board of Revenue dated 9/92 (Annexure-L) but nevertheless again recommended for releasing the disputed machinery at the exempted rate. But the Chairman, National Board of Revenue put his foot down."

33. On this point, the learned Assistant Attorney-General for the respondent relies on the unreported judgment dated 4-6-2001 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petitions No. 344 and 345 of 1995, wherein their lordships decided as under:

"Customs, laws and rules are for the Customs Authority. This power is not necessary for encouraging investment for establishing industries. The liability to pay customs duties and taxes is remotely linked, if at all, with the questions of encouraging investment or establishing industrials. We have discussed above the relevant sections of the Biniog Board Ain, 1989, dealing with the functions and powers of the Board of Investment. As we have seen above, these sections have not committed any power to the Board of Investment to determine the tax liability of an industry in respect of its import."

34. It appears that the Appellate Division decided that the decision of Bol is to be implemented for implementation of a project in due time.

35. We have earlier quoted the order of Bol and it appears that Bol passed full order with detailed reasons and specifying the goods to be exempted from payment of duties and taxes in case of the Sarina. Accordingly, NBR issued the order in case of the Sarina.

36. But in petitioner's case the order of Bol (annexure-E to the writ petition) reads as under:

"উপযুক্ত বিষয়ে ইউনিক হোটেলে এন্ড রিসোর্টস লিঃ এর নিকট হতে প্রাপ্ত ২৭-৮-২০০১ তারিখের একটি স্বব্যখ্যায়িত আবেদনটি এতসঙ্গে সংযুক্ত ক্রতঃযচিত বিষয়ে প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করার জন্য নির্দেশক্রমে অনুরোধ করা হল।উল্ল���খ্য যে, শিল্প প্রকল্পেটি আমেরিকা বিনিয়োগকারীর সাথে যৌথ বিনিয়োগ "পাচতারা হোটেল" শিল্প খাতে প্রস্তাবিত প্রকল্পহিসাবে বিনিয়োগ বোর্ড কর্তৃক বিনিয়োগ প্রাপ্ত।"

<u>37. From this letter it is evident that BOl in its own order did not specify the goods/machineries for which exemption from duties and taxes are to be given. It rather forwarded the application of petitioners for necessary action. Therefore, it cannot be said that BOl directed NBR to exempt the duties and taxes by specifying machineries as was the case of the Sarina. Therefore, NBR is not legally bound to comply with this vague letter. Moreover, BOl did not also mention that such exemption facilities is necessary for implementation of the project in time as observed by the Appellate Division in the case reported in 17 BLD (AD) 83 = 51 DLR (AD) 36. Furthermore, the facts and circumstances of the said case is completely distinguishable and, as such, it is not applicable in this case.</u>

38. Thus, we do not find any merit in the submissions of the learned Advocates for the petitioner rather, we find merit and force in the submissions of the learned Assistant Attorney-General for the respondent.

39. In view of the discussions made in the forgoing paragraphs vis-a-vis the law, we find no merit in this rule.

<u>40. Before parting with the judgment, we would like to note that although it is not the subject matter of the writ petition but it came to our notice that in case of the Sarina, BOl used the vague words" "..........অন্যান্য যন্ত্রপাতি" which is not proper BOl must specify in its order the machineries for which exemption of duties and taxes may be given. It is an important issue, as it is connected with revenue income of the Government and so, BOl must be careful about the "words/language used" in its letter/order.</u>

41. In the result, the rule is discharged.

The respondents are at liberty to encash the bank guarantee furnished by the petitioner.

No order as to costs.

End.
